review_mode: Fresh independent read-only source review; Bash restricted to python3 scripts/check_docs.py. No target score supplied to the reviewer.

assessment.verdict: Ship. At the manifest heads this is a coherent, verifiable release-support change: four cohesive roots, machine-gated coverage of all 26 resources and 27 data sources, environment-only credentials, preserved state addresses and safe defaults, and newcomer documentation whose substantive provider-behavior claims I was able to confirm against the released provider's implementation and schema rather than against implementer assertions. All six round-2 findings are genuinely fixed, and the new scripts/check_docs.py converts three of those defect classes (duplicate release section, stale test count, broken heading fragment, drifted receipt hashes, uncovered cleanup types) into repeatable gates; my independent run of it recomputed every receipt's exact .tf hash set and passed. Evidence is honest: the live report and receipts positively confirm what was exercised, explicitly scope the archived-workspace 403 reads, and list unexercised onboarding/shared-rule/external-secret/deployment/MCP operations rather than implying validation. Four residual P3s remain, none blocking: one documented null-fallback path is unexecuted everywhere and uses nonsensitive() outside try() (the only item with real failure potential, on an opt-in path), the new cleanup gate pools type coverage per product rather than per variant so the exact round-2 gap class could recur undetected, docs/validation.md under-describes its own gate, and two Gateway create_workspace prerequisites lack the negative runs their Supply Chain counterparts now have.
assessment.score_rationale: Correctness (high): every HCL/schema pairing I checked matches the released provider — workspace scope_name/scope_management required and count-gated, runtime_api_key.auth_code required and sourced from the sensitive deployment-profile item, api_key_name's 31-char limit mirrored by the <=27 name_prefix validation, override reason change producing replace (matching the receipt's delete+create), rule original_state baseline, instance full-PUT/write-only/ephemeral wiring, and dlp_profiles.total_count being a returned-page count (datasource_dlp_profiles.go:113) exactly as the README states. One latent risk only: nonsensitive() applied outside try() on a documented-nullable count. Coverage (very high): coverage.py fails on any unmapped released type and the table resolves 27 data + 26 resource rows to real configuration, with optional/import-only paths carrying precise prerequisites; all four routing patterns, AIRS plus deterministic denial, managed/external workspace, Skill trust/catalog/results, opt-in shared-rule adoption with baseline restoration, and protected import-first onboarding are present. Ownership/credential protection (excellent): validate.py scrubs PANW_/TF_VAR_/TF_LOG and pins a direct{} installation; prevent_destroy guards both adopted objects with documented state-rm release paths; the key/app deletion cascade is respected by using a disposable scanner app and rejecting its separate adoption, and the receipts independently confirm the cascaded app absent; sensitive material stays in sensitive outputs with only a row count declassified; sanitization scan passed over 448 files and tfvars/state are gitignored. Docs usability (strong): each README teaches start, use, update, cleanup and troubleshooting, with boundaries stated rather than hidden; evidence lives in separate sanitized files. Testing/evidence (strong, bounded): 17 mock runs including one mocked apply proving the after-write lookup, 13 Python tests, hash-gated receipts, and type-level independent cleanup rows — weakened by per-project pooling in the gate, by 403-inaccessible rows counting as covered, and by necessarily partial live coverage that is disclosed. Deductions are small and all P3; nothing I found is a user-visible break on a default path.

findings.title: Documented null-when-unavailable path of trust_override_matches is unexecuted and calls nonsensitive() outside try()
findings.explanation: skills.tf:44 computes `nonsensitive(try(length(data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_overrides.owned[0].result.skill_overrides), null))`, and both skills.tf:43 and examples/ai-supply-chain-security/README.md:36 promise the value is null when the lookup is unavailable. That fallback branch is never executed anywhere in the evidence set. The mock suite's only degraded-response run, `missing_native_rule_list` (tests/features.tftest.hcl:75-88), scopes its override_data to data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_rules.catalog[0] and asserts only output.skill_rule_count == null; the file-level mock_data at tests/features.tftest.hcl:2-4 always supplies result = { skill_overrides = [{}] }, so every other run takes the populated branch, and the live Supply Chain run read the key successfully (receipts:163). The structural concern is the operator order: the provider marks this data source's `result` sensitive (internal/products/supplychain/skill_data.go:45 sets Sensitive for kind == "overrides"), so in the normal case length() is sensitive and nonsensitive() is required, but in the fallback case try() yields a plain unmarked null and nonsensitive() receives a non-sensitive value. Because the data source carries depends_on the trust write, the read is deferred to apply, so if that call rejects an unmarked argument the failure lands mid-apply after the override has been created, with a function-argument diagnostic instead of the documented null. I could not execute Terraform under this review's tool restrictions, so I am reporting the verifiable part — an unexecuted documented path on an opt-in lesson — rather than asserting the error; see boundaries. effective_skill_rule_count (skills.tf:38) has the same documented nullability and the same absence of a regression run, so skill_rule_count is the only one of the three count outputs whose null contract is actually proven.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the declassification inside the error guard so the branch is safe under either nonsensitive() semantics: `value = var.enable_skill_scanning ? try(nonsensitive(length(data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_overrides.owned[0].result.skill_overrides)), null) : null`. Then add one mock run mirroring missing_native_rule_list that uses override_data on data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_overrides.owned[0] (and, in the same run, data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_rule_instances.effective[0]) with values = { result = {} } and asserts output.trust_override_matches == null && output.effective_skill_rule_count == null, updating the gated count in docs/validation.md:7 and README.md:74 to 18.

findings.title: New cleanup gate pools independent-check coverage per product, so neither Gateway variant is gated individually
findings.explanation: check_docs.py:56-59 builds `checked` as the set of types from every receipt cleanup row whose `project` equals the run's project, then subtracts it from that run's managed_resource_types. Both Gateway runs use project "ai-gateway" (receipts:185 and :328), so the two variants share one pool and the per-variant `variant` labels added this round (receipts:569 and :702) are never read by the gate. Reproducible trigger: delete the owned-workspace runtime-profile row at receipts:564-570 — the existing-workspace row at :696-703 still satisfies the owned run, and `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` still passes. That is precisely the per-variant gap reported in round 2, so the gate as written cannot prevent its recurrence. A second, smaller effect: a row whose outcome is "workspace archived; child read forbidden (HTTP 403)" (receipts:461-550) counts as covered identically to "absent", so the gate's printed message about "cleanup type coverage" does not distinguish positively verified absence from an inaccessible read. The published prose at docs/live-runs/provider-0.10.0.md:19 does caveat the 403s correctly, so this is a gate-strength issue rather than a misleading claim.
findings.recommended_fix: Key the coverage set on (project, variant): require each cleanup row that belongs to a multi-variant project to carry `variant`, and compute `checked = {row["type"] for row in receipt["cleanup"]["checks"] if row["project"] == run["project"] and row.get("variant", run["variant"]) == run["variant"]}`. Optionally also report counts of positively-absent versus inaccessible outcomes in the summary line so the gate's message cannot be read as proof of absence.

findings.title: Canonical evidence index omits the new documentation/evidence gate from its description of scripts/validate.py
findings.explanation: docs/validation.md:42 enumerates what `python3 scripts/validate.py` checks: "formatting, locked provider installation, schema validation, mock feature tests for all four projects, release coverage, and Python helper tests". scripts/validate.py:34 also runs scripts/check_docs.py, which is the gate this round introduced and the one that enforces the single release section, the recorded test count against test source, every receipt's exact .tf hash set, and cleanup type coverage. README.md:74 lists it ("documentation links/evidence hashes") and ci/README.md:3 lists it, so docs/validation.md is the one place that under-describes it — and it is the document the root README and all four product READMEs point newcomers to for "Recorded live results and their limits". Reproducible trigger: compare docs/validation.md:42 against the subprocess calls in scripts/validate.py:19-35; the sample-input fmt check at :20-24 is likewise unmentioned. A reader auditing which claims are machine-enforced would conclude the hash/link/count gates are not part of the local gate.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend docs/validation.md:42 to match scripts/validate.py, for example: "...mock feature tests for all four projects, release coverage, documentation links and heading targets, recorded test counts and live source-hash/cleanup receipts, and Python helper tests without tenant access or remote writes", and note that the CI matrix runs neither the coverage gate, the documentation/evidence gate, nor the Python suite.

findings.title: Gateway's two create_workspace prerequisites have no negative mock run, unlike their Supply Chain counterparts
findings.explanation: workspace-variables.tf:13-17 requires an explicit workspace_scope_name when create_workspace is true, and :53-57 requires non-null workspace_default_metadata. Neither condition is exercised: the only negative Gateway run is reject_ambiguous_workspace (tests/features.tftest.hcl:46-54), which supplies both of those inputs and targets var.workspace_id, while owned_workspace, external_scope and owned_workspace_without_discovery all supply workspace_default_metadata = {} and a scope name. Reproducible trigger: set create_workspace = true and omit workspace_scope_name in a scratch run — the targeted guidance fires, but nothing in the suite would notice if the condition were weakened or the try(...) guard at :14 regressed to an evaluation error on null. This matters only because the Supply Chain root adopted the opposite, better convention this round: its three lookup prerequisites now have reject_lookups_without_skill_scanning covering all three in one run, and manage_skill_rule has reject_missing_rule_identity. The Gateway's own owner-facing guidance at README.md:58-75 treats these two inputs as the central prerequisites of the new workspace lesson, so they deserve the same regression floor.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one run to examples/ai-gateway/tests/features.tftest.hcl that sets workspace_id = null, create_workspace = true and workspace_default_metadata = {} while omitting workspace_scope_name, with expect_failures = [var.workspace_scope_name], and a second that supplies the scope name but omits the metadata, with expect_failures = [var.workspace_default_metadata]. Then update the gated count in docs/validation.md:7 and README.md:74, which check_docs.py:43-46 enforces against the test sources.

assessment.validation_assessment: Validation quality is high and, unusually, mostly self-enforcing. Offline gate (offline-final.log, reproduced in part): four locked roots init/validate/test clean against the signed Registry 0.10.0 package, 17 mock runs (5 Gateway + 1 Red Team + 4 Runtime + 7 Supply Chain) exactly matching the `run` blocks I counted in source, coverage of 26 resources/27 data sources recomputed from `terraform providers schema -json` so the table cannot drift, and 13 Python helper tests. scripts/validate.py:13-18 strips PANW_*/TF_VAR_*/TF_LOG from the environment and pins TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE to a `direct {}` installation, which is the strongest credential-protection control in the change set: it makes credentialed or dev-override validation structurally impossible, not merely discouraged. The single mocked apply (tests/features.tftest.hcl:24-39) is the right escalation for the after-write trust lookup, and all providers are mocked with mock_data defaults, so no tenant write occurs; the assertion output.trust_override_matches == 1 proves the dependency wiring and declassification, not service semantics. My own run of scripts/check_docs.py independently recomputed all five receipt hash sets against the current .tf files and 21 Markdown files' link and heading targets, so the "exact final HCL" claim is verified rather than accepted. Live evidence is proportionate and honestly bounded: five fresh runs on 2026-10-04 each record create/empty-plan/update/refresh-only/empty-plan/destroy plus empty state, with independent API reads recorded per type. The owned-workspace variant's children are correctly reported as 403-inaccessible after archival rather than as proven absent (provider-0.10.0.md:19), the owned workspace and IAM scope are positively matched, and both variants' Runtime profiles now have all-revision inventory checks. The runtime key/app cascade is verified by an extra cleanup row for prisma-airs_runtime_customer_app even though no customer_app was managed — exactly the right check for that hazard. Unexercised operations (shared-rule adoption, instance onboarding, instance reads, external-secret retrieval, hybrid installation, fresh MCP invocation, existing-app import) are enumerated at provider-0.10.0.md:57-63 and mirrored in per-run `boundaries` flags, and historical 0.9.0 results are explicitly not relabeled. Optional configurations are sensible and schema-backed: every optional path I traced resolves to real released attributes with correct presence/sensitivity, gated by count/flags with cross-field validations and, for the two destructive-adoption paths, prevent_destroy plus documented state-rm release procedures. The main residual weaknesses are the gate's per-project pooling of cleanup types, the equal treatment of 403 and absent outcomes inside that gate, and two unexecuted degraded-response paths (overrides and rule_instances null fallbacks) plus two untested Gateway variable prerequisites. The Docusaurus side is gated rather than asserted: check_content.py now validates skill-onboarding as the eighth complete configuration, navigation.spec.ts now routes the three new example pages, and 63 Registry plus 54 exact schema pages are checked against the built provider.
unverified_boundaries: Terraform's nonsensitive() behavior on an unmarked argument was not executed: my tools permitted only `python3 scripts/check_docs.py`, so I could not run terraform console/plan to determine whether skills.tf:44's try(...)→null fallback errors or returns null. The finding is scoped to the verifiable fact that the branch is unexecuted in both the mock suite and the live run; the failure mode is stated as conditional.

The null/degraded-response path for data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_overrides and data.prisma-airs_supply_chain_skill_scanning_rule_instances was never taken: the live tenant returned the native keys and the file-level mock_data always supplies skill_overrides, so only skill_rule_count's null contract is empirically proven.

Gateway owned-workspace child cleanup rests on an archived-workspace inference plus Terraform's empty state; only the workspace (admin archived-list UUID match), the owned IAM scope (404/410) and the Runtime profile (all-revision inventory) are positively verified for that variant. Per-instance absence beyond the receipts' type-level rows is not established.

Shared Skill rule adoption, Skill instance onboarding and the instance data read, external-secret retrieval, hybrid deployment installation, fresh MCP tool discovery/invocation, and existing customer-app import were explicitly not live-exercised. Their correctness rests on released-schema validation plus mock plans; I confirmed attribute names, presence and sensitivity against the provider schema and implementation, which does not establish service-side acceptance of the payloads.

The Gateway owned-workspace plus enable_platform_discovery combination was only mock-planned (the live owned run had discovery off and read no data sources), so the singular workspace lookup against a freshly created workspace and the 13-family page counts in that mode are unverified live.

Mock provider values are schema-shaped but synthetic; assertions such as length(keys(output.platform_page_counts)) == 13 and output.trust_override_matches == 1 prove configuration wiring and declassification, not API semantics or pagination completeness.

I did not execute terraform, go test, or the docs-site suite. The offline-final.log, docs-check-final.log, provider-local-roots.log and sanitization-check.txt outcomes (including the 98 validated HCL examples, 63 Registry pages, 54 exact schema pages, 11 navigation and 9 parity browser tests, and the 448-file credential scan) are taken as reported; I independently reproduced only scripts/check_docs.py.

The receipts' sanitization was assessed only from the published files; I did not read private credentials, state, plans or private evidence, so I cannot independently confirm that the placeholder substitutions correspond to the real tenant identifiers.

Provider repository verification was limited to the released docs, schema definitions and the implementation paths my claims depended on (security profile Delete, skill data-source sensitivity, dlp/deployment-profile total_count, api_key and workspace schemas). I did not audit the full provider at head; the manifest states its head is unchanged since the prior completed review.

check_docs.py's heading-slug derivation approximates GitHub's anchor algorithm (it strips non-word characters and numbers duplicates from zero), so exotic headings could in principle produce a slug mismatch the gate would not flag; none of the 21 current files exhibited this.
